subject: Logging priorities and exception catalog for security asks
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Alex Davidson <alex.davidson@cresthealth.com>
Cc: security@cresthealth.com
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Logging priorities and exception catalog for security asks

Alex / team — looping you in on the internal triage for the asks you sent last week. High level: CrestHealth sent three discrete requirements that map to different product workstreams and potential exceptions. I want to align on what we can commit to short-term vs. what needs a formal exception.

Summary of asks (from CrestHealth intake form, attached):
- Retention: 7 year archival window for a subset of activity types (PHI-related inference logs).
- BYOK/KMS: Customer-managed keys with quarterly rotation and escrow/escrow-ops documentation.
- Audit logs: Finer-grained write/read access events (per-tenant API key binding + admin console events).
- SSO: SAML assertions must include department attribute and login-origin metadata (they flagged GCP Identity-aware proxies).

Questions for the group:
1) Which of these are product features we can schedule (and roughly when)?
2) Which require architecture changes that force an exception path for this customer?
3) What evidentiary artifacts can we provide in the meantime (screenshots, partial logs, attestation) while we implement?

Proposed short-term plan:
- Triage retention and audit-log granularity as candidate "product" items for Q3 roadmap; propose temporary carve-out for retention window via export + S3 escrow.
- BYOK: if we can offer a VPC/private deployment + KMS integration, consider limited pilot but document that rotation/escrow will be manual for now.
- SSO attributes: engineering to validate whether our SAML attributes pipeline can be extended; if not, provide guidance to Crest on AD/GCP mapping.

Can Marissa weigh in on prioritization and required product scope? Jonas — can you sketch feasibility and estimate (ballpark) for the features above? Alex — what is Crest comfortable treating as a temporary exception vs. a blocker?

Attachments: crest_req_form.pdf (their intake), ksm_escalation_matrix.xlsx (internal risk matrix).

Thanks — KP

--
Kimberly Park
Director, Security Programs
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Alex Davidson <alex.davidson@cresthealth.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Logging priorities and exception catalog for security asks

Thanks Kimberly — good summary. A few clarifications from product:
- Retention: supporting a 7-year window for PHI is a heavy commitment. We can offer exports and a managed archival flow as a near-term deliverable (Q3-Q4) but full integrated long-term storage with search/indexing for that window is a Q4+ initiative.
- Audit logs: we can add more event types (console admin, API key lifecycle) as a configuration toggle. That work is medium effort — estimate 3 sprints once we have definitive schema.
- BYOK/KMS: product prefers scoped pilot on Redwood Private; Dedicated might support a managed KMS integration but escrow workflows and legal requirements will need SRE + Compliance signoff.
- SSO attributes: this is likely low product effort if it's only adding department and login-origin to assertions; need to confirm with IAM whether attribute release is safe for multi-tenant accounts.

Proposed asks for Crest (quick wins):
1) Provide Crest an export + ingestion playbook for long-term retention (we'll own the export automation).
2) Turn on additional audit event collection for their tenant (toggle, then we iterate schema).
3) For BYOK: propose Redwood Private pilot and a manual rotation/escrow process for the first 90 days.

I'll add this as a candidate to the Product backlog and attach the short spec. Jonas — if you can give rough engineering cost estimates, I'll tag priority and we can push a canary pilot.

Marissa
Product Lead, Security & Compliance

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Alex Davidson <alex.davidson@cresthealth.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Logging priorities and exception catalog for security asks

Quick feasibility notes from infra/serving runtime:
- Retention: exporting keys+logs to S3 (encrypted) is trivial; the challenge is the search/index UX for multi-year windows — that requires a separate infra tier (cost + compliance). For a pilot we can do export + customer-managed S3 with lifecycle rules. Estimate: 2 engineer-weeks to implement export automation and access docs, 6-8 weeks for an indexed archival tier.
- Audit logs: adding event types + wiring to current audit pipeline is low-medium effort. We need the final schema from Product; after that it's ~3 sprints to fully populate events and add per-tenant flags.
- BYOK/KMS: supporting quarterly rotation with customer-managed keys introduces operational load. We can integrate with customer KMS (Cloud KMS, Azure KeyVault) for key wrapping — low-level support exists. Escrow (storing recovery copies) needs legal & compliance policy; we need a defined escrow owner. Technical estimate: 4-6 sprints (incl. CI, rotation automation, and key provenance logs).
- SSO attributes: if it's only adding department/login-origin to SAML assertion, we can do it in a patch (1 sprint) but need to ensure attribute values are normalized and won't leak cross-tenant info.

Blockers/asks from infra:
- Product to deliver final event schema and retention scoping per-event type.
- Compliance/legal to sign off on escrow policy for BYOK before we enable customer uploads.
- Ops to confirm runbook for rotation/incident story.

I'll queue the export automation as a high-priority spike. If Crest can accept the export+escrow pilot, we can move quickly.

— Jonas
Senior Staff Engineer, Runtime

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Alex Davidson <alex.davidson@cresthealth.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2026 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Logging priorities and exception catalog for security asks

Thanks all — quick decision log and next steps so we have a single source of truth: 
1) Short-term pilot (target: start week of Jun 21): export-based retention for PHI logs into CrestHealth-managed S3 (Redwood to automate exports + verification).
2) Audit logs: Marissa to finalize schema by Jun 14; Jonas to begin event wiring spike the week of Jun 14. Deliverable: per-tenant audit toggle and sample event set by end of July.
3) BYOK: Offer Redwood Private pilot with manual escrow for first 90 days. Compliance/legal: Kimberly to coordinate with Legal for escrow contract language and responsible parties.
4) SSO attributes: Jonas will validate attribute release with IAM and deliver a safe-guarded patch (ETA: 1 sprint).

Action owners and immediate asks:
- Marissa: Add the Crest spec to Product backlog and send final schema link to Jonas by Jun 14.
- Jonas: Start export automation spike and post notes in the Drive link below.
- Kimberly: Draft initial escrow language and loop Legal; schedule a 30-min alignment call with Crest (proposed Jun 15 10:00 PT). Alex — please confirm whether that time works for your team.

Drive notes: https://drive.redwood.internal/notes/cresthealth-compliance-2026
Jira ticket: SEC-4821

If nobody objects, I'll mark this as an "exception-pending" path for Crest and document the pilot acceptance criteria.

Best — KP

--

Redwood Inference
